canonical_data: session transcripts, session index, configuration, skills, and MCP declarations under ~/.kimi-code, with sessions resumable, forkable, and exportable
current_repo_note: Reviewed at HEAD d4b9dc4 (2026-10-14). The VSCode extension carries its own Apache-2.0 file and the pi-tui package keeps its upstream MIT notice from the earendil-works/pi fork; the managed Kimi Code service is a login path, not a deployment of this record.
strengths: Provider configuration is documented per integration: the managed Kimi service, Anthropic, OpenAI chat and responses interfaces, Gemini, Vertex, and third-party OpenAI-compatible endpoints with a models.dev-assisted import
Sessions persist locally with resume, fork, export, and context compression, and all runtime data lives under one relocatable directory with locked-down credential files
Built-in coder, explore, and plan subagents run in isolated contexts, and lifecycle hooks let the user gate risky tool calls with local commands
Telemetry properties pass through a scrubber that redacts emails, URLs, tokens, keys, and file paths before anything leaves the machine
weaknesses: The primary path is the vendor's managed service and models, so the open client mostly matters as a Moonshot AI front end unless the user configures other providers
Telemetry runs by default with an environment-variable off switch rather than a first-run choice, which the data-sovereignty reading counts against it
1,570 open issues against five months of history signal fast adoption and a substantial unresolved support burden
Video input, the plugin marketplace trust levels, and the forked TUI's drift from upstream are documented surface the review did not independently exercise
why_it_matters: Moonshot AI's open coding CLI pairs a tuned terminal agent with subagents, hooks, and editor protocol support across many model providers.
